= Kobiton-managed routing for virtualUSB
:navtitle: Kobiton-managed virtualUSB routing

// Generated by Robot Ranch (Ledger) from KOB-52679. Draft for docs-team review.
// Source: KOB-52679

== Overview

Kobiton-managed routing makes virtualUSB traffic for a host machine reachable without manual IP address management. Kobiton sets up routing when virtualUSB is enabled on the host machine and removes it when virtualUSB is turned off.

== Availability

* Available to organizations subscribed to virtualUSB.
* Organization admins configure routing on the *virtualUSB* tab of the host machine *Settings* dialog in *Device Management*.
* *Managed by Kobiton* appears as a routing option only when Kobiton-managed routing is available for the organization.

// REVIEWER NOTE: Confirm deployment availability (Cloud, Hybrid, Standalone). The 4.27.0S
// release notes exclude the virtualUSB tab as not yet available on Standalone.
//
// REVIEWER NOTE: The Jira ticket does not say what an admin does when *Managed by Kobiton*
// is not offered. Confirm whether to direct admins to Kobiton Support.

== How routing works

Each host machine with virtualUSB enabled uses one of two routing options:

*Managed by Kobiton*::
Kobiton provisions and removes routing for the host machine automatically.

Self-managed::
The organization manages routing and the connection address. Saving a self-managed host machine does not change Kobiton routing.

// REVIEWER NOTE: Confirm the exact UI label for the self-managed routing option.

Kobiton provisions routing when virtualUSB is enabled on a host machine that uses *Managed by Kobiton* routing.

Kobiton removes routing when either of the following happens:

* virtualUSB is turned off on the host machine.
* The host machine changes from *Managed by Kobiton* to self-managed routing.

// REVIEWER NOTE: The Jira release summary states that active virtualUSB sessions on the host
// machine end before routing is removed. The Jira development notes list graceful session
// termination as deferred, and the test notes do not cover it. Confirm before documenting.

== Provisioning status

After the settings are saved, routing provisioning is in progress until routing is ready. When provisioning completes, virtualUSB is enabled on the host machine.

If provisioning fails:

* virtualUSB is turned off on the host machine, and the host machine shows a failed provisioning status.
* Enable virtualUSB on the host machine again to retry.

If Kobiton cannot start provisioning when the settings are saved, the save returns an error and the previous settings are restored for every host machine in the save.

// REVIEWER NOTE: Confirm the UI labels shown for the in-progress, complete, and failed
